rationale: This is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived "Self-Funding Cash Stock Value" and "Liquid Platform Productivity Value" (identical oibdp/(cogs+xsga) productivity leg, with the numerator's oancf/xsga merely swapped for oibdp−xint), so it adds no new economic content.

Structurally identical to the archived "Cash-Buffered Sales Productivity" with sale→revt−cogs and che/at→che/(at+dlc), which are trivial denominator/numerator tweaks rather than a substantive response to the diagnosed FMB-vs-alpha divergence.

It overlaps heavily with the archived "Short-Debt Coverage Liquidity Value" on the cash-to-enterprise-value leg, but charging both interest and expensed R&D against operating profit on assets is a genuinely different quality hurdle not yet tested in this archive, so it is worth one run.

The valuation leg is plain earnings-to-price (a long-published anomaly) and the quality leg is internally inconsistent — oibdp/(|pi|+xint) is mechanically maximized by firms with near-zero pretax income, i.e. it rewards exactly the non-core/transitory-earnings firms the hypothesis claims to exclude.

Near-duplicate of the archived "Intangible Platform Glamour Fade" (same market-cap-over-intangible-platform ratio times negated margin), with cash added to the denominator and the margin denominator changed — a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal.

Coherent and directionally consistent, but it is the third pass at the archive's leverage×weak-profitability family (Debt-Overhang Profit Drain, Current-Debt Interest Trap) and largely re-expresses the well-known distress/leverage anomaly without diagnosing why those predecessors delivered negative alpha alongside positive FMB slopes.
